checkpoint_review: The Router correctly identified the species as a Brown Pelican and accurately flagged the 'Wings... contrasting lighter body' checkpoint as false, since this specific morph has a dark body. However, the Router was too lenient on the 'Legs are short and webbed...' checkpoint, marking it N/A. While the legs are tucked, the feet/toes are clearly visible extending behind the tail in the image; thus, the structural integrity of the feet (webbing/fusion) is testable and should have been evaluated rather than dismissed. The Router also missed evaluating the 'fingered' wing tips against the OVD hint regarding AI fusion, though it noted softness in artifacts.
artifact_review: The Router identified texture anomalies at wing tips and blur at the water interface. I agree with the wing tip assessment but elevate the severity: the primary feathers exhibit significant 'melting' and lack distinct separation, appearing as a fused mass rather than individual digits—a common AI failure mode confirmed by the OVD hint. The Router's observation of blur at the lower body is valid but underestimates the issue; there is a distinct 'ghosting' or double-exposure artifact where the feet/tail meet the water, suggesting temporal inconsistency or generation error. The Perceptual Quality Auditor found only slight compression, but the visual evidence of structural melting at the wingtips is a more severe generative artifact than simple compression.
alignment_reasoning: Strong semantic alignment with Brown Pelican morphology. Expert classifiers confirm 'pelican' with high confidence. One checkpoint failed due to species-specific coloration (correctly handled). Alignment is high, but not perfect due to the unverified leg checkpoint which was actually visible.
artifact_reasoning: Significant structural artifacts at wingtips (fused/melted primaries) exceed the Router's 'soft texture' description. Ghosting/double-image artifact at the tail/water interface indicates generation instability. These structural defects lower the artifact score below the formula baseline.
